eslint toolchain. This override swaps the one vulnerable copy that can be
whose engines ('20 || >=22') still allow our pinned Node 20.13.1.
Three things that look like fixes and are NOT — all tested, not guessed:
1. A blanket brace-expansion override. v5's CommonJS entry exports
{ expand }, not the function, so minimatch@3's require() call throws
3. @eslint/config-array@^0.23.5 (which would drop one more advisory by
moving to minimatch@10). It requires Node ^20.19 || ^22.13 || >=24, and
this project is pinned to Node 20.13.1 — CI's 'node-version: 20' would
resolve a newer Node than the dev machine and hide the mismatch.
What remains: eslint@9 -> minimatch@^3.1.2 -> brace-expansion@1, whose
latest 1.x IS the vulnerable version. There is no patched 1.x. The only
real fix is eslint 10, a major bump deliberately deferred. See ci.yml.
